messages.subject: Re: repair error/crash
messages.body_plain:
The 'repair' function was developed at the time when featureCounts was slow in dealing with location-sorted paired-end reads. But we have made dramatic improvement on the speed of featureCounts in counting location-sorted paired-end reads and featureCounts can now count location-sorted reads at almost the same speed as it does for name-sorted reads. So you do not need to run 'repair' function beforehand anymore.

But we will get this bug fixed in the next release.

Regards,

Wei

messages.subject: Re: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature
messages.subject_clean: reciprocal overlap of reads and genomic feature
messages.body_plain:
Hi
It sounds great.
Currently I am using Bedtools intersect developing my pipeline.

But while doing that I am missing another option which even Bedtools is missing (in addition to other features present in featurecount).
Basically i have features with length size 18-300 bp. If I will allow overlap fraction 0.95 then the reads and features with length 18 bp has to overlap exactly. But for length 300 bp there is a freedom of +/- 15 bp.
If I want to have some matching freedom for 18bp reads/features then for +/-2bp i need to use overlap fraction 0.888. But for length 300 it would be about +/- 35 bp which is too much.
But I am interested to give some freedom for matching even for short reads/features. For example trancription start in bacteria is not 100% exact,often it is +/- 1bp and it would be good if you can allow number of bp not the fraction (fraction means more +/- bp for longer reads/features).

Therefor I have been thinking about option where you can set number of allowed non-overlaping positions and maximum non overlapping from this option and '−−fracOverlap' would count. Eg '--maxNonOverlapPos' and '--maxNonOverlapPosFeature' (default should be 0).

Here would be an example how it should work:

Reads in bam:
name start end
r1    1     16
r2    1     15
r3    1     18
r4    1     20
r5    1     21
r6    1     280
r7     1    290
r8    1     299
r9    1     300
r10    1     301
r11    1    310
r12   1    320

Features in SAF
Name start end
f1   1    18
f2   1   300

--maxNonOverlapPosFeature 0 --maxNonOverlapPos 0 −−fracOverlapFeature 1 −−fracOverlap 1#only exact matches
*f1 will match:
r3 -exact match
*f2 will match:
r9 -exact match

--maxNonOverlapPosFeature 2 --maxNonOverlapPos 2 −−fracOverlapFeature 1 −−fracOverlap 1 #feature and reads can differ by 2 bp
*f1 will match:
r3 -exact match
also r1, r4 as 2 bp nonmatch is allowed
*f2 will match:
r9 -exact match
also r8, r10 as 2 bp nonmatch is allowed

--maxNonOverlapPosFeature 0 --maxNonOverlapPos 0 −−fracOverlapFeature 0.95 −−fracOverlap 0.95 #feature and reads can differ by fraction 0.95
*f1 will match:
r3 -exact match
*f2 will match:
r9 -exact match
also r7,r8, r10,r11 as overlap fraction is 0.95

--maxNonOverlapPosFeature 2 --maxNonOverlapPos 2 −−fracOverlapFeature 0.95 −−fracOverlap 0.95 #feature and reads can differ by fraction 0.95
*f1 will match:
r3 -exact match
also r1, r4 as 2 bp nonmatch is allowed
*f2 will match:
r9 -exact match
also r7,r8, r10,r11 as overlap fraction is 0.95

messages.subject: BAM file being sorted by featureCounts despite `--donotsort` [v1.5.3]
messages.subject_clean: BAM file being sorted by featureCounts despite `--donotsort` [v1.5.3]
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to use featureCounts to count reads in 1-kbp bins tiling the entire genome for some downstream CNV calling. The input data are paired-end BAM files from whole genome sequencing, so they're quite large (200+ GB). Accordingly, I would prefer to avoid re-sorting the BAM files, as it adds significant overhead in terms of time and disk usage. I would be okay with the trade-off of considering paired reads individually.

However, when I added the --donotsort option, I noticed that featureCounts is still generating a sorted BAM file (i.e. *.sam.fixbam). Is this expected? I'm using featureCounts v1.5.3.  Here's the command I'm running:

> featureCounts -a windows.1000.saf -F SAF -o output.read_counts.ws_1000.tsv --donotsort -O --largestOverlap --ignoreDup -s 0 -T 12 input.bam

Cheers,
Bruno

messages.subject: Re: BAM file being sorted by featureCounts despite `--donotsort` [v1.5.3]
messages.subject_clean: BAM file being sorted by featureCounts despite `--donotsort` [v1.5.3]
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bruno,

I tested the "--donotsort" option and it worked appropriately.

The ".fixbam" file you've seen in the directory is the temporary BAM file for fixing the format of your input BAM file; it wasn't for sorting. As I know, featureCounts needs to fix the BAM files from STAR and Picard because an alignment record in these BAM files can go into two or even more BAM blocks (each ~ 64kb after decompression).

Cheers,
Yang
